shortDescription: An inheritable Storageborn xenotype: nomadic, sapient living furniture with randomized body forms, age-based carrying capacity and armor, and configurable refuge recruitment.
body:
## Storageborn xenotype
- Adds inheritable xenotype `omw_storageborn`, the `OMW_Storageborn` membership gene, the `OMW_StorageHead` head gene, fourteen randomized body genes, and five age-stage genes.
- Requires Biotech, Harmony, and Big and Small - Genes and More (`redmattis.bigsmall.core`); loads after Harmony and Big and Small, and before `mlie.10xcarryingcapacity`.
- The membership gene suppresses visible tattoos and uses `StoragebornGene.PostAdd` to apply Storageborn setup and select one enabled body gene.
- The xenotype is non-combatant and inheritable. Its gene package supplies Big-and-Small universal diet, no clothing/armor, no equipment, unliving and reproductive traits, resilience, no blood, pain resistance, animal affinity, naked speed, temperature/toxic resistance, sleeplessness, robust health, sensory limitations, and strong/poor skill aptitudes. It is not added to default combatant generation pools.
- Vanilla thought nullifiers are patched so Storageborn are not penalized by many apparel, beauty, sleeping, food, social-insult, title-room, or corpse-related thoughts.
- The custom head gene renders `Head/StoragebornHead` through `PawnRenderNode_AttachmentHead`, uses bald/no-beard filters and Big-and-Small's facial disabler, and ships the runtime-requested `Head/StoragebornEye` texture. Body genes disable facial animations and select directional artwork through Big-and-Small `PawnExtension.bodyPaths`.

## Body forms and category settings
- Defines six extensible `StoragebornCategoryDef`s: Neolithic, Medieval, Industrial, Spacer, Ultra, and Archotech. Current body genes are Luggage, Mimic, Cardboard, Maid, Cube, Treant, Golem, Suitcase, Wardrobe, Orb, MechLoader, Cube2, Robot, and Robot2; each has a category extension and directional textures under `Textures/Storageborn/Bodies/`.
- The controller discovers categories and body genes from loaded defs, allowing compatible mods to add more categorized body genes without code changes.
- The mod settings window has Bodies, Storage carrying capacity stages, and Refuge quest tabs. Body settings support optional World Tech Level integration (`m00nl1ght.WorldTechLevel`): when available, matching is enabled by default and only categories at or below the current world tech level are effective.
- With world matching disabled, category mode is used by default; category toggles enable or disable all bodies in a category. Individual body toggles are available when category mode is disabled. Turning world matching off clears disabled categories and bodies, re-enabling the full discovered pool.
- A body-status window reports each discovered body's effective state and reason (world-tech filtering, category setting, individual setting, or missing category). The effective pool controls initial randomization, rerolling, and quest pawns.
- The stage tab edits five offsets and factors and applies them to `CarryingCapacity` plus `VEF_MassCarryCapacity` when that optional stat exists. Saved settings are persisted through `ModSettings`/Scribe.

## Body randomization and lifecycle
- Adding the membership gene removes all existing discovered Storageborn body genes and adds one randomly selected effective body gene as an endogene. If no body is enabled, no replacement is selected.
- The Bodies tab can rerandomize every Storageborn pawn found on maps, in caravans, and in the alive/dead world-pawn collection, deduplicating pawns encountered in multiple collections.
- Applying Storageborn setup assigns the fixed `OMW_StoragebornChildhood` backstory, removes currently worn apparel from babies, and recalculates age-stage genes and armor-stage genes. The current implementation does not assign a Wanderer adulthood backstory.
- A Harmony postfix on `Pawn_AgeTracker.BirthdayBiological` recalculates both the size/carrying stage and the natural-armor stage for Storageborn pawns.
- Stage genes are mutually exclusive and inactive unless the pawn has the Storageborn membership gene. The implemented developmental thresholds are: baby or under 8 uses stage 0/Dwarfism; children from 8 use stage 1/Small; adults from 18 use stage 2/Medium; age 30 uses stage 3/Large; age 50 uses stage 4/Gigantism; age 70+ also maps to stage 4. Stage genes adjust carrying capacity, and stages 0/1 exclude Tiny and reduce market value.
- Armor stages independently select Big-and-Small armor genes by the same six index slots: `BS_ToughSkin`, `BS_ToughSkin`, `BS_NaturalArmor`, `BS_NaturalArmor`, `BS_NaturalArmor_Great`, and `BS_NaturalArmor_Great`.

## Refuge quest
- Adds a settings-gated `OMW_StoragebornWanderer` incident with a standard `WandererJoin`-style quest root. It uses normal incident selection and standard accept/reject/timeout behavior; there is no custom first-day timer.
- The generated wanderer is assigned `omw_storageborn`, then receives Storageborn setup and the normal effective body randomization. The quest is enabled by default and can be disabled in the Refuge quest settings tab.

## Debugging, assets, and documentation
- Dev action `Pawns -> Spawn Storageborn Lifecycle` spawns player-owned test pawns at biological ages 0, 8, 18, 30, 50, and 70, then logs a result.
- The mod includes localized settings strings in `Languages/English/Keyed/Storageborn.xml`, a Workshop preview/icon, directional body/head textures, compatibility notes, known-issue notes, and an AI-assisted development disclosure.
- Compatibility documentation identifies World Tech Level and Pick Up and Haul support, warns that 10x Carry Capacity can negate the base carrying-capacity behavior, and lists other carry/facial-animation mods as untested. Known notes include weapon/clothing restrictions, limited usefulness of capacity without inventory mods, baby onesies, and ideology-mask exceptions.
